hints: Focus on what makes a termination step different, two free radicals joining together to cancel each other out.
Work out which radicals are present here, you get $\text{Cl}^{\bullet}$ from chlorine and $^{\bullet}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl}$ after a hydrogen is abstracted from $\text{CH}_{3}\text{Cl}$.
Try joining those radicals in pairs and see which pairing gives a stable two-carbon molecule with two chlorines.
walkthrough:
**Recall the free radical substitution mechanism**

This is chlorination of $\text{CH}_{3}\text{Cl}$ by $\text{Cl}_{2}$ in UV light. It goes by initiation, propagation, then termination.

Initiation:
$$\text{Cl}_{2} \xrightarrow{uv} 2\text{Cl}^{\bullet}$$

**Identify the propagation radicals**

In propagation, a chlorine radical removes H to make a new carbon radical, which then reacts on.
$$\text{Cl}^{\bullet} + \text{CH}_{3}\text{Cl} \rightarrow ^{\bullet}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$$
$$^{\bullet}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}_{2} \rightarrow \text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl}_{2} + \text{Cl}^{\bullet}$$
So the two radicals floating around are $\text{Cl}^{\bullet}$ and $^{\bullet}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl}$.

**Apply what termination means**

Termination is radical + radical combining to form a stable molecule with no new radical. Let's list them:
$$\text{Cl}^{\bullet} + \text{Cl}^{\bullet} \rightarrow \text{Cl}_{2}$$
$$^{\bullet}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}^{\bullet} \rightarrow \text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}$$
$$^{\bullet}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl} + ^{\bullet}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{CH}_{2}\text{ClCH}_{2}\text{Cl}$$

**Pick the termination product from the options**

That last combination joins two chloromethyl radicals to give 1,2-dichloroethane, $\text{CH}_{2}\text{ClCH}_{2}\text{Cl}$. That is a classic termination dimer product.

options.A: HCl is formed in the first propagation step when Cl radical abstracts H from CH3Cl. Propagation makes a new radical to continue the chain, so it is not termination.
options.B: CH2=CH2 (ethene) contains no chlorine and has a double bond. There is no C2H3 radical or elimination route here to make it, and radical combination forms single bonds, not alkenes.
options.C: CH2ClCH2Cl is formed when two .CH2Cl radicals combine in termination: .CH2Cl + .CH2Cl gives CH2ClCH2Cl. Two radicals are removed and a stable molecule is made, exactly what termination means.
options.D: H2 is not formed. There are no H. radicals in this system to combine, the hydrogen ends up as HCl in propagation. Students sometimes guess H2 because H atoms are removed, but they never exist as free H. here.
